title: Single-step purification of intrinsic protein complexes in Saccharomyces cerevisiae using regenerable calmodulin resin
author: Bhojoo, Biggar

steps.title: Grow TAP‑tagged yeast culture
steps.instruction: Inoculate the TAP‑tagged Saccharomyces cerevisiae strain (from glycerol stock or YPD‑agar plate) into 5 mL sterile YPD liquid medium in a 15 mL tube and grow overnight at 30 °C, 250 rpm. Then inoculate 5 mL of this overnight culture into 40 mL YPD in a 100 mL flask and grow overnight at 30 °C, 250 rpm. Finally add 10–20 mL of the overnight culture to 300 mL YPD and grow at 30 °C, 250 rpm until the optical density at 600 nm reaches 1.0–1.2.

steps.title: Harvest and wash cells
steps.instruction: Transfer the 300 mL culture to clean centrifuge bottles and spin 5 min at 5000 rpm. Discard the supernatant without disturbing the pellet, add 10 mL cold distilled water (4 °C) and resuspend by swirling or pipetting. Transfer the suspension to a 50 mL conical tube, centrifuge 5 min at 3000 rpm, 4 °C. Discard supernatant and wash the pellet twice: first with 10 mL cold distilled water, then with 10 mL IPBL buffer (no protease inhibitor). Briefly invert the tube on a paper towel to remove residual liquid, flash‑freeze the pellet in liquid nitrogen and store at –80 °C.

steps.title: Grind‑based cell lysis
steps.instruction: Break the frozen flask tube with a hammer, transfer the frozen pellet to a coffee grinder together with a similarly sized dry‑ice pellet and grind for ~30 s. Transfer the resulting powder to an ultracentrifuge tube and resuspend in 10 mL cold calmodulin‑binding buffer (4 °C) containing 25 µL CaCl₂ and a protease‑inhibitor cocktail. Centrifuge at maximum speed for 1 h at 4 °C; keep the supernatant for the purification step.

steps.title: Alternative glass‑bead lysis (optional)
steps.instruction: Resuspend the frozen pellet in ~200 µL lysis buffer (50 mM Tris‑HCl pH 8.0, 1 % DMSO, 100 mM NaCl, 1 mM EDTA, 1 mM PMSF, 1 µg/mL leupeptin, 1 µg/mL pepstatin A). Add 1–3 g pre‑washed glass beads per gram of pellet, vortex 3–5 times for 1 min intervals on ice. Centrifuge 5000 rpm for 10 min at 4 °C and transfer the supernatant to a new tube. Add ~200 µL calmodulin beads to a 15 mL tube, wash the beads twice with 1X calmodulin‑binding buffer and discard the wash. Incubate the supernatant with the beads at 4 °C with gentle rocking for 3 h to overnight (optimal 5 h). Centrifuge 3000 rpm, 4 °C for 5 min and discard the supernatant.

steps.title: Wash and elute bound proteins
steps.instruction: Cut the tip of a pipette to avoid breaking the resin. Wash the beads twice with pre‑chilled (4 °C) 300 µL 1X calmodulin‑binding buffer containing protease inhibitors, then wash twice with 300 µL 1X calmodulin‑wash buffer. Elute the bound proteins in three fractions of 200 µL 1X calmodulin‑elution buffer into fresh 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tubes. Analyze eluates by SDS‑PAGE.

steps.title: Regenerate calmodulin‑agarose beads
steps.instruction: Transfer the used beads to a clean 1.5 mL tube (beads can be reused at least three times). Dialyze 3 h to overnight in snake‑skin dialysis tubing against 0.1 M carbonate buffer pH 7.9 containing 2 mM EGTA. Wash beads three times with 300 µL 1 M NaCl containing 2 mM CaCl₂, then three times with 300 µL 0.1 M acetate buffer pH 4.4 containing 2 mM CaCl₂. Equilibrate the beads with 200 µL calmodulin‑binding buffer for 2 h. For long‑term storage, keep beads at 4 °C in 20 % (v/v) ethanol.
